record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Topological Algebra
record.original_question: Does every topological group arise as a quotient group of a zero-dimensional topological group of the same weight, and under what conditions is an almost metrizable topological group a quotient of a zero-dimensional group of the same weight? Here a space X is zero-dimensional when dim X = 0, and a topological group is almost metrizable when it contains a compact subset of countable character.

evidence.quote:
Problem 1 (Choban). Is every topological group a quotient group of a zero-dimensional topological group of the same weight? When an almost metrizable topological group is a quotient of a zero-dimensional group of the same weight?
A space X is zero-dimensional if dim X = 0. A topological group is almost metrizable if contains a compact subset of countable character.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a topological space $X$ is zero-dimensional if $\dim X = 0$ (the covering dimension is zero). A topological group $G$ is almost metrizable if it contains a non-empty compact subset of countable character in $G$ (equivalently, a compact set with a countable base of neighborhoods in $G$). The weight $w(G)$ of a topological group is the minimum cardinality of a base for its topology.

(a) Is it true that every topological group $G$ is topologically isomorphic to a quotient group $H/N$ of some zero-dimensional topological group $H$ with $w(H) = w(G)$, where $N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $H$?

(b) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on an almost metrizable topological group $G$ under which $G$ is a quotient group of a zero-dimensional topological group $H$ with $w(H) = w(G)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return decisive evidence that this question (attributed to Choban) about realizing every topological group, and in particular every almost metrizable topological group, as a quotient of a zero-dimensional topological group of the same weight has been resolved. Related work by Choban and others on zero-dimensional topological groups exists, but the specific weight-preserving quotient question appears to remain unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: The local properties in topological groups and related concepts and questions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems related to Choban concerning zero-dimensional topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys still discuss Choban-type problems on zero-dimensional topological groups as open.
